Den automatiska huggspårsanalysen delar: The automatic groove analysis now splits the runes by where the strokes stand along the runic band, for all stones and not only staveless ones. This gives 70 sure links instead of 28, 61 of them between Swedish runestones, and four of Jarlabanke's stones now hang together. The links find 40 per cent of the stones that runologists have tied together (Williams 1990), and 92 per cent of the links stand in his groups. The way of counting was chosen after seeing that list. Språkdraget æftiR eller at räknade at ba: The language trait æftiR or at counted at only when a name followed directly, while every æft- word counted as æftiR. That missed at as the second preposition, for example “… ok Fastlaug at bonda sinn”, and hit some districts more than others. Both words are now counted the same way, and the older short form aft/æft is counted separately. The trait changed on 237 runestones, and the statistics have been recomputed. The error was found while reading Lena Peterson's 1996 article on exactly these words.

With the old borders the differences in language become sharper and point to the folklands – r for ʀ in Fjädrundaland, at against Attundaland – while the cross and the prayer become less certain when Uppland is divided. The folklands' hundreds agree with the six-year tithe of 1314, and each parish's hundred is taken from ISOF's place-name register.

Vi prövade ristarmodellen mot runologern: We tested the carver model against the runologists' own judgements in Runor 2020 of which stones were made by the same hand. It did not give the same carver more often than neighbouring stones do, and it can only choose among named carvers. The suggestions in the Stone overview are therefore now called suggestions among known carvers, and no suggestion is called strong any more without independent evidence. The new evidence, similarity beyond the neighbours, compares the stone's text with the stones around it and recognises the runologists' own groups much more often than neighbours do. It is shown for every stone, and stones that resemble another stone without a carver are marked as a possible unnamed hand.
